meta.disclaimer: Not legal advice. These are counts from each state court system's published statistics, kept for marketing planning. A case filed is a new case on a court's docket (in Texas, a new case or motion), not a person or a client. Check the state's current report.
meta.notice: Probative is a marketing firm, not a law firm; not legal advice.

changes.summary: West Virginia added: circuit, family and magistrate courts in all 55 counties, calendar year 2025, from the Supreme Court of Appeals' Annual Statistics Report (728 records: general civil, small claims, felony, misdemeanor, divorce, other domestic relations, protective orders, juvenile, adoption, guardianship, mental health).

Oregon added: circuit courts in all 36 counties, calendar year 2025, from the Oregon Judicial Department's Cases Filed report (444 records: landlord-tenant, small claims, general civil, felony, misdemeanor, violations, divorce, other domestic relations, protective orders, juvenile, probate, civil commitment).

Pennsylvania added: courts of common pleas in all 67 counties, calendar year 2024, from the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts county caseload reports (1,156 records: injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, contract and debt, landlord-tenant, foreclosure, criminal, protection from abuse, support, custody, divorce, juvenile, adoption, guardianship).

Virginia added: circuit, general district and juvenile and domestic relations district court filings for calendar year 2025 by locality, read from the Supreme Court of Virginia's caseload PDFs (2227 records).
New field fips on every record: the 2-digit state FIPS code on a state row, the 5-digit county FIPS code (or codes, where one court serves a city and a county together) on a county row.
Wisconsin read from the state's official file (1095 records).
Indiana read from the state's official file (1664 records).
Maryland read from the state's official file (425 records).
Washington read from the state's official file (600 records).
